title: Rear Disc Brake: Diagnostic Starting Point
introduction:
At the rear disc brakes, hydraulic pressure makes the calipers press pads against rotating discs. The resulting friction slows the wheels and generates heat. The rear brakes belong to a shared hydraulic system, so a symptom's apparent location is a clue rather than a verdict.

I begin by separating noise, pedal feel, pulling, drag and vibration, then describing the operating condition. ABS can produce noise and pulsation while active, but that possibility is no universal alibi for brake complaints. Use the required brake-system diagnostic referral below to continue. This page contains no test setup, measurements or result branches and cannot serve as a standalone diagnosis.

edits.text: For rear disc brake diagnosis, refer to [Brake System](#/document/G1721936) (206-00 Brake System - General Information, Diagnosis and Testing).
edits.why: The system-level diagnostic path matters because hydraulic operation and electronically controlled pressure changes can affect what the driver hears or feels. The symptom alone does not establish which component needs attention.
